chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Gangsters in Kansas City
summary: Kansas City gangsters made Basie work without pay; a Kirk singer nearly got killed; the Luscoe brothers had the band afraid to fetch their beer.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Rough in what way, Mary Lou?

It was during the Prohibition and a little bit of everything was happening in Kansas City. Certain people did exactly what they wanted to do. It was during the time when all the gangsters was really a big thing. I've heard people speak of gangsters in New York. Well, they were kids to the ones I've worked for. Count Basie and our band worked for some gangsters in Kansas City. Before I joined the band they made Count Basie work without pay for one or two weeks. Andy Kirk came in next.
Why did they make him work without pay?
If you angered them their temper was terrible. If you angered them in any way.
What was the pay like then in Kansas City?

I don't think it was very much. I hadn't joined the band then. I heard that Count Basie had to work either one or two weeks without pay. Andy Kirk's band went in next and we had a singer with us and he got in a dispute with one of the gangsters there. The gangster looked at
him and he says, "Andy, if it wasn't for you I'd kill him!"
Oh, sure he meant it, sure. We worked for the Gershwin brothers.

No, that isn't the - I've forgotten their name. The Luscoe brothers. They were pretty well to the point to, had to be careful. I remember once after playing they told the boys, "Let's go out and play softball." Whoever wins had to go back to the club and get a keg of beer. Naturally the boys won and the Luscoe brothers looked for them and they had gone home, because they were afraid to go back and pick up the beer.
